key: Scaling up is moving the whole shop
name: ch00_scale_up_vs_out
alt: A split scene: on the left a shopkeeper moves his whole kirana shop into a bigger building, on the right he opens several side-by-side counters whose clerks must agree on stock.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, the same middle-aged kirana shopkeeper (late 40s, white kurta, grey moustache, reading glasses on a cord) appearing in both halves. LEFT panel: a small shop with its rolling shutter pulled half down and a handwritten board reading "closed for shifting"; the shopkeeper and a helper push a loaded handcart of rice sacks and biscuit tins toward a taller three-storey building, and beyond it, at the edge of the panel, the street simply ends at a fence with no taller building in sight. His face is tired and doubtful. RIGHT panel: the same shopkeeper stands behind one of four identical small counters set side by side under one long awning, each with its own young clerk in a blue apron and a short queue of customers with cloth bags; the four clerks lean toward each other shouting and comparing notebooks, a dotted arrow loops between the counters with tiny inset bubbles showing a stock register and a price tag, signalling that they must keep agreeing. Bright late-morning light on the left feels slightly gloomy and dusty, the right side busy and lively. Labels: "SCALE UP" at the top of the left panel, "SCALE OUT" at the top of the right panel, and "AGREEING" in small caps along the dotted arrow joining the counters.

key: This book opens the bonnet: the engine
name: ch00_open_the_bonnet
alt: A mechanic opens a car bonnet to show the engine and gearbox, while the dashboard and satnav inside the car are greyed out.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a small roadside garage in an Indian town, with a corrugated tin roof, a calendar on the wall and a tyre leaning against the doorway. A compact hatchback car sits in the centre with its bonnet propped open. A young mechanic (mid 20s, grease-stained navy overalls, a rag over his shoulder, focused and friendly) leans in and points with a spanner at the engine block, which is drawn clean and detailed: cylinders, belts and a cutaway showing stacked metal plates like shelves. Below and behind the engine a gearbox is visible in a cutaway, with three gear wheels and thin lines running from it to all four wheels of the car, showing power being shared out. A curious engineer customer (early 30s, half-sleeve shirt, ID lanyard, holding a cup of chai) peers over the mechanic shoulder. Through the windscreen the dashboard and a satnav screen are visible but drawn in pale, faded grey, deliberately out of focus, with a small "skip" tag hanging from the rear-view mirror. Warm afternoon light slants into the garage, calm and curious mood. Labels: "STORAGE" with a thin leader line to the engine, "DISTRIBUTION" with a thin leader line to the gearbox and its lines to the wheels.

key: never opens a box and doesn
name: ch01_warehouse_and_shopfront
alt: A shop counter at the front takes customer orders while a warehouse worker behind it stores and fetches sealed labelled boxes without opening them.
scene: A cutaway side view of a single building split into two rooms, front and back, seen from slightly above like a dollhouse. FRONT room on the left: a bright shop counter where a smart shop manager (early 30s, maroon sari with a name badge, holding an order slip) talks with two customers; behind her a chalkboard menu of items and a small tray of order slips. A hatch in the wall connects to the BACK room on the right: a tall warehouse with steel racks reaching the ceiling, each shelf holding identical brown sealed cardboard boxes taped shut, each with only a small white label such as "1042" or "R-7". A warehouse worker (late 40s, khaki uniform, cap, calm and methodical) slides one sealed box onto a trolley; the box is drawn with packing tape intact and a tiny padlock icon to show he never opens it. Dotted arrows flow from an order slip through the hatch to the worker and a box coming back to the counter. Neutral indoor light, orderly and clean. Labels: "DBMS" above the shop counter room, "STORAGE ENGINE" above the warehouse room.

key: The teller (OLTP) handles thousands
name: ch01_teller_vs_analyst
alt: A bank branch where a teller serves a fast queue of small deposits while an analyst upstairs studies large charts drawn from the same ledger.
scene: A wide cutaway of a two-level Indian bank branch seen from the front. GROUND floor: a long counter with glass partitions and a brisk teller (late 20s, crisp white shirt, tie, quick hands) stamping deposit slips; a long, fast-moving queue of customers in everyday clothes holds tiny slips, one reading "₹500", and small speed lines show the queue moving quickly. Behind the teller sits a large green cloth-bound ledger on a stand. UPPER floor, connected by a glass mezzanine: a thoughtful analyst (early 40s, spectacles, cardigan over a shirt) sits at a long desk covered with big printed charts, bar graphs grouped by city and a pie chart, slowly sipping tea, with only two or three huge question cards pinned on a board behind him. A thick dashed line runs from the ledger on the ground floor up to the analyst desk, showing he reads the same live book. Calm daylight from tall windows, contrast between the busy bustle downstairs and the quiet study upstairs. Labels: "OLTP" next to the teller counter, "OLAP" next to the analyst desk, and "HTAP" placed on the dashed line connecting the ledger to the upper floor.

key: Row-wise is one card per student
name: ch01_class_register_rows_columns
alt: A teacher compares a stack of per-student report cards with three separate sheets for names, roll numbers and marks.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle, set on a teacher desk in an Indian school staffroom with a ceiling fan and a steel almirah in the background. The same teacher (mid 40s, cotton sari, spectacles pushed up on her head, a red pen) appears in both halves. LEFT panel: she hands a single cream-coloured card to a smiling schoolboy in a white shirt and navy shorts; the card shows a small photo square, a name line, roll number and a short marks list, and a neat stack of similar cards sits beside her, one card per student. RIGHT panel: she sits with three long paper sheets laid side by side, one full of names, one full of roll numbers, one full of marks; she runs her red pen straight down the marks sheet only, with a small calculator showing a single average and a pencil-drawn arrow sweeping down the column. The other two sheets are pushed slightly aside, untouched. Soft morning light, orderly and studious mood. Labels: "ROW STORE" at the top of the left panel, "COLUMN STORE" at the top of the right panel.

key: A diary where you never use an eraser
name: ch01_diary_never_erase
alt: A man writes corrections as new lines in a pen diary instead of erasing, and later copies only the valid lines into a fresh diary while the old one goes in the bin.
scene: A wide desk-level view of a small study table by a window, the scene read left to right as a short story. On the left a young man (late 20s, grey t-shirt, ink pen, relaxed) writes in a thick diary; the open pages show many short lines, several struck through lightly, and a fresh line at the bottom reading "cancel entry 4", with an eraser lying on the table crossed out by a small red X to show it is never used. A tiny inset bubble above the page highlights two lines about the same item, the lower one circled with a note "latest wins". In the centre, a curved arrow with a small clock icon leads to the right side, where the same man, now later in the evening with a desk lamp switched on, copies only a few clean lines from the fat old diary into a slim new diary; the old diary, bulging and full of crossings, drops into a cane wastepaper basket. Warm lamp light on the right contrasts with daylight on the left. Labels: "APPEND ONLY" above the diary on the left, "COMPACTION" above the copying scene on the right.

key: An in-place structure is a whiteboard
name: ch02_whiteboard_vs_notebook
alt: One person wipes and rewrites a number on a whiteboard while another writes a new line in a pen notebook instead of erasing.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, inside a small startup office with plants and a window. LEFT panel: a young woman (mid 20s, mustard kurti, hair in a bun) stands at a whiteboard holding a duster in one hand and a marker in the other; she has just wiped one cell of a small table and is writing a new number in exactly the same spot, with faint smudge marks around it, a curved arrow showing the old value being wiped away. RIGHT panel: a young man (late 20s, black hoodie, round glasses) sits at a desk with an open hardbound notebook and a pen; the earlier line is left untouched and a new line is written on the next empty row, with a small sticky arrow on the margin pointing to the newest line marked "current". Bright, even office daylight, focused and calm mood. On the wall between the two panels hangs a small clock, and on a shelf behind the young man several older filled notebooks stand in a row, untouched since they were written. Labels: "IN PLACE" at the top of the left panel, "IMMUTABLE" at the top of the right panel; the left panel is slightly highlighted with a soft glow to show it is the chapter focus.

key: A binary tree makes you drive to a new
name: ch02_dictionary_across_town
alt: A comparison of a man driving between many small buildings, one per question, versus asking many questions inside one big building.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided horizontally, top and bottom, showing an aerial map view of a small Indian town with roads, a temple and a water tank. TOP panel: a tired man (30s, helmet, kurta, sweat on his brow) rides a scooter along a winding route that stops at many tiny one-room buildings, each holding a single page of a dictionary on a stand; the route zigzags with numbered stop pins 1 to 9 and continues off the edge, showing endless trips. BOTTOM panel: the same man has parked once outside one large library building; a cutaway reveals him inside at a long table with many dictionary pages spread out, a row of small question-mark bubbles above him being ticked off one after another, smiling and relaxed, with a single parking icon outside. The top panel feels hot and hurried with dust trails, the bottom calm and cool with shade. In the top panel a small fuel gauge on the scooter sits near empty and a clock tower shows the hours passing; in the bottom panel the same clock shows only minutes have gone by. Labels: "BINARY TREE" at the left edge of the top panel, "WIDE NODE" at the left edge of the bottom panel.

key: is a building directory. The signs
name: ch02_building_directory
alt: An office building where signboards in the lobby and on each floor only point the way, and the actual offices sit along the ground row.
scene: A clean front cutaway of a tall office building, like a dollhouse section, arranged so the lobby is at the top and the offices form the bottom row. At the top, a lobby with a large directory signboard showing three arrows with short ranges; a visitor (early 30s, beige shirt, holding a file folder) reads it. Stairs lead down to a middle floor with two smaller signboards, each with arrows pointing further down. At the very bottom runs a long row of small office cubicles side by side, each with a door, a nameplate and a person working inside (a tailor, an accountant, a lawyer, a travel agent), and short corridors linking each office to its neighbour. A dotted path traces the visitor route from the lobby sign, down one staircase, past one middle sign, into one bottom office. A painter on a ladder near the lobby sign holds a brush but is idle, sipping tea, showing that changing an office does not require repainting signs. Bright, clean daylight, orderly mood. Labels: "INTERNAL NODES" beside the signboards, "LEAVES" along the bottom row of offices.

key: A full drawer in the catalogue room
name: ch02_full_drawer_split
alt: A library clerk moves the back half of the cards from an overflowing drawer into a new drawer and adds a label to the cabinet.
scene: A close, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an old wooden card catalogue cabinet in a quiet library, with tall bookshelves softly blurred behind. A librarian (early 50s, cotton sari, glasses on a beaded chain, careful hands) stands at the cabinet. On the left, one drawer is pulled out and overflowing, index cards bursting upward. In the centre, she lifts the back half of the cards in a thick bundle, a curved arrow showing them moving into a brand-new, lighter-coloured empty drawer on the right that still has a price tag string on its handle. On the cabinet top she is sticking a small new label tag on the index card holder reading "13 →". In a small inset bubble in the top corner, a taller cabinet above shows the same thing happening one level up, with a tiny plus sign for a new top level. Warm reading-room light from a high window, careful and satisfying mood. A few readers sit at long tables in the background with books open, unaware of the reshuffle, and a small step stool stands beside the cabinet for reaching the higher drawers. Labels: "SPLIT" above the moving bundle of cards, "SEPARATOR KEY" pointing to the new label on the cabinet.

key: Disk is a parking lot you paint yourself
name: ch03_hotel_vs_parking_lot
alt: A hotel front desk hands out rooms on request, while a man paints parking bays himself and tracks empty bays in a notebook.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a tidy hotel lobby with a polished front desk, a brass bell and a key board behind; a friendly receptionist (late 20s, uniform blazer, name badge) hands a room key card to a traveller with a trolley bag, a small sign behind showing room sizes, effortless and smiling. RIGHT panel: an open-air dusty parking lot under the sun; a man (40s, vest and rolled-up trousers, cap, paint bucket and long roller) is painting white bay lines himself on the asphalt; a clipboard at his feet shows a hand-drawn grid with some bays ticked. In the lot a large truck is just driving out, leaving a big empty gap between two small hatchback cars, and the man pauses to point at that gap with a thoughtful look, a dotted outline marking it as reusable space. Cool, calm indoor light on the left contrasts with hot bright sun on the right. Labels: "MEMORY" at the top of the left panel, "DISK" at the top of the right panel, and "FREE SPACE" in small caps inside the dotted gap.

key: To add a book in the middle you slide
name: ch03_shelf_sliding_books
alt: A man straining to slide a row of heavy books along a full shelf to make room for one new book in the middle.
scene: A front-on, eye-level view of a long wooden bookshelf with no gaps, books neatly sorted by title, set in a small home study with a window to the right. A man (mid 30s, checked shirt with sleeves rolled up, sweat on his brow, determined expression) holds one new book in his left hand at the middle of the shelf, while with his shoulder and right arm he pushes a long row of thick, heavy encyclopaedia-like volumes one slot to the right. A series of small curved motion arrows above every book to his right shows that each one has to shift, and the last book on the far right is teetering at the edge of the shelf. A small thought bubble above him shows a stack of dumbbells, hinting at how much lifting this is. On the floor a few already-shifted books lean against each other. Warm afternoon light through the window, slightly comic, effortful mood. On the left side of the shelf, the books before the insertion point stand perfectly still and neat, drawn in calmer colours to show that only the right-hand side has to move. Labels: "INSERT" above the new book in his hand, "SHIFT EVERYTHING" along the row of arrows to the right.

key: guests sitting wherever there
name: ch03_guest_list_slotted_page
alt: A host updates an alphabetical guest list on a clipboard while a new guest takes the next free chair without anyone moving.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a small wedding reception hall decorated with marigold garlands and fairy lights. In the foreground stands a host (late 30s, cream kurta with a Nehru jacket, smiling) holding a clipboard; the clipboard shows a short alphabetical list of names, and he is writing a new name squeezed between two existing names, with a small caret arrow marking the insertion. In the background, rows of white plastic chairs with guests sitting in arrival order, not alphabetical: an aunty in a green sari, an older uncle with a walking stick, two young cousins on phones. A newly arrived young man (mid 20s, blue shirt, gift box in hand) is being seated in the next free chair at the end of the row, with a dashed arrow from his name on the clipboard to his chair. Nobody else is moving; the other guests are relaxed and chatting. Warm festive evening light. A small table near the entrance holds a stack of gift boxes and a steel plate of sweets, and a child in a little sherwani peeks curiously at the clipboard from behind the host. Labels: "SLOTS" pointing at the clipboard list, "CELLS" above the row of seated guests.

key: A checksum is counting the boxes
name: ch03_checksum_vs_crc
alt: A delivery check where one worker counts boxes and another inspects a continuous seal tape across all the boxes.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle, set on a warehouse loading dock with a small delivery truck backed up. LEFT panel: a delivery supervisor (late 40s, khaki shirt, clipboard, pencil behind the ear) counts a stack of five cardboard boxes with his finger, ticking numbers; one box is clearly missing from a dotted outline and he notices it with a raised eyebrow, but two boxes with swapped address labels sit right in front of him and he does not notice, shown with a tiny swap arrow between their labels. RIGHT panel: the same stack of boxes is wrapped by one long continuous strip of red seal tape running across every box; a young inspector (late 20s, high-visibility vest, checking with a torch) points at a small torn section of tape that clearly shows a break, and she looks alert. Neutral, even daylight from the open shutter. In the background, a forklift parked near a stack of pallets and a hand truck leaning against the wall suggest a busy dock, and a small wall clock shows early morning delivery time. Labels: "CHECKSUM" at the top of the left panel, "CRC" at the top of the right panel.

key: Anyone can see the free gap from the
name: ch04_shelf_with_clipboard
alt: A warehouse shelf with boxes stacked from the back and index cards pinned from the front, with a clipboard at the front showing where the free gap is.
scene: A side cutaway view of one long warehouse shelf, seen at eye level so its full depth runs left to right. At the right end, against the back wall, sealed brown boxes are stacked and growing toward the left. At the left end, near the front, small white index cards are pinned in a row on a narrow rail, growing toward the right. Between them is a clear empty middle gap, highlighted with a soft dotted bracket. Hanging on the front post of the shelf is a clipboard. A warehouse supervisor (early 40s, navy polo shirt, reading glasses, relaxed) stands at the front and simply reads the clipboard, without walking along the shelf; a dotted sight-line goes from the clipboard to the gap. A younger worker in the background carries one more box toward the back stack. Clean industrial lighting from overhead tube lights, orderly mood. The clipboard itself is drawn clearly with two short lines, one with a small arrow pointing to the end of the cards and one pointing to the start of the boxes, so the gap can be read at a glance. Labels: "OFFSETS" above the row of index cards, "CELLS" above the stack of boxes, "FREE SPACE" inside the dotted gap.

key: leaves a slip in the pigeonhole
name: ch04_pigeonhole_overflow
alt: An office mailbox wall where a parcel too big for a pigeonhole is replaced by a slip pointing to the back room.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an office reception wall covered with a grid of identical narrow wooden pigeonholes, each with a small name strip. Most pigeonholes hold a few envelopes neatly. In the foreground an office assistant (early 30s, pale blue salwar kameez, ID lanyard) is placing a small folded paper slip into one pigeonhole, while a large parcel too wide to fit sits on her trolley. To the right, an open doorway leads to a back room with metal shelving where the same big parcel is shown sitting on a shelf numbered "3", and a dashed arrow runs from the slip in the pigeonhole to that shelf. A colleague (late 20s, shirt and trousers, coffee mug) collects his ordinary letters from his own pigeonhole happily without needing the back room. Bright, neat office lighting, calm and efficient mood. A wall clock and a small potted money plant sit above the pigeonhole wall, and the back-room shelf holds a few other oversized parcels, each with a matching small number tag. Labels: "FIXED SLOT" under the pigeonhole wall, "OVERFLOW PAGE" above the back-room shelf.

key: Hansel and Gretel. You don
name: ch04_breadcrumbs_path
alt: Two children walk into a forest dropping breadcrumbs, then pick them up in reverse order on the way out, with no arrows painted on trees.
scene: A wide forest scene seen from slightly above, with a winding path from a small village house at the bottom left into tall trees at the top right. Two children walk along it: a girl (about 9, braided hair, red frock) and a boy (about 11, striped t-shirt and shorts), each with a small cloth bag. On the way in, the girl drops pale breadcrumbs one by one at each fork, drawn as a neat dotted trail with numbered crumbs 1, 2, 3, 4. At the top right deep in the forest a small treasure chest glows, the destination. A second ghosted pair of children in a softer tone walks back on the same path, picking up the crumbs in reverse order 4, 3, 2, 1 and dropping them into a pouch. Some tree trunks along the path have empty wooden signboards with a faint red cross over them to show no painted arrows are needed. Dappled green forest light, gentle storybook mood. Small birds perch on branches watching but do not eat the crumbs, and the path forks several times so the crumbs clearly mark exactly which branch the children took at each fork. Labels: "PATH STACK" along the breadcrumb trail, "NO PARENT POINTERS" near the crossed-out signboards.

key: A night cleaning crew in an office
name: ch04_night_cleaning_crew
alt: A night cleaning crew tidies office desks and writes free desk numbers on a whiteboard, while a power cut threatens to wipe the board.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an open-plan office at night, lit by a few overhead lights and city lights through large windows. Two cleaners (one woman in her 40s in a blue uniform sari with the end tucked at the waist, one young man in a grey uniform) move between desks: one stacks scattered old papers neatly into a bin, the other wipes an empty desk. Several desks are clearly unused, chairs tucked in, a small green tick on each. At the office entrance stands a whiteboard where the woman writes desk numbers in a list, "12, 17, 23". In a small inset bubble at the top right corner, the same whiteboard is shown in darkness during a power cut, its list wiped blank, with the unused desks behind it sitting dim and forgotten under a tiny cobweb. Quiet, calm night mood with cool blue tones and warm desk lights. A cleaning trolley with a mop bucket and a bin bag stands in the aisle, and a desk lamp still glows on one empty desk where someone forgot to switch it off before leaving. Labels: "COMPACTION" above the cleaners at the desks, "FREELIST" above the whiteboard, "LEAKED" inside the power-cut inset.

key: You can only fit four folders on the
name: ch05_desk_and_filing_cabinet
alt: A clerk works on four folders at a small desk next to a tall filing cabinet, filing a scribbled folder back before it leaves the desk.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a small government-style office with a ceiling fan and a wall calendar. On the left a small wooden desk holds exactly four coloured folders, spread out, with no room for a fifth; a clerk (late 30s, half-sleeve white shirt, spectacles, pen behind ear) sits at it. On the right stands a tall grey steel filing cabinet with many drawers. The clerk holds a fifth folder he has just taken from the cabinet, looking at the full desk. One of the four folders on the desk has red pen scribbles on its cover and a small red dot; a curved arrow shows the clerk carrying that scribbled folder back into an open cabinet drawer first, with a small stamp mark, before he can lay down the new one. A faint dotted outline in the cabinet shows the old stale copy being replaced. Warm, slightly dusty office light, methodical mood. A chai glass is balanced precariously on the edge of the crowded desk, and a small sticky note on the cabinet shows the drawer the folder came from so it goes back to the same place. Labels: "PAGE CACHE" above the desk, "DISK" above the filing cabinet, "DIRTY" next to the scribbled folder.

key: A night guard walking a circle of
name: ch05_clock_guard_eviction
alt: A night guard walks a circular corridor of offices switching off lights and clearing offices whose lights were already off.
scene: A top-down, slightly tilted view of a circular corridor with eight small office rooms arranged in a ring, like a clock face, in a quiet building at night. A night guard (50s, khaki uniform, cap, torch in hand, calm face) walks clockwise around the ring, with a dotted circular arrow showing his route. Each room has a light switch by its door. Some rooms glow yellow because someone used them today; as the guard passes one, he flips its switch off. One room ahead of him is already dark; a cleaner with a trolley is emptying it, with a small broom icon. Two rooms are tinted grey with a person still working at a desk inside under a lamp, and the guard walks past them without touching the switch. Cool blue night tones with warm yellow office light. At the centre of the ring sits a small security cabin with a logbook on its table and a lamp, and footprints on the corridor floor show the guard has already completed many earlier rounds. Labels: "CLOCK HAND" next to the guard, "EVICT" over the dark room being cleared, "PINNED" over one of the grey occupied rooms.

key: Before changing anything in the pot
name: ch05_chef_notebook_wal
alt: A chef writes each change in a notebook before touching the pots; after he faints, a second chef reads the notebook to restore every pot.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, inside a busy restaurant kitchen with steel counters and big pots on gas burners. LEFT panel: a head chef (40s, white chef coat, tall hat, thick moustache) writes in a small spiral notebook propped on the counter, the visible line reading "pot 7: +2 tsp salt", while his other hand holds a salt spoon paused over pot 7; numbered pots 5, 6 and 7 steam on the burners. RIGHT panel: the same chef sits slumped on a stool in the corner, dizzy with stars around his head, while a younger chef (late 20s, chef coat, bandana) holds the notebook and reads it carefully, setting each pot back to the right state; one half-finished dish is being tipped into a bin with a small curled undo arrow. The notebook pages show only additions, nothing erased. Warm, steamy kitchen light. Shelves of spice tins line the back wall, and in the right panel the notebook pages are shown slightly enlarged so the reader can see entries running in order, numbered one after another. Labels: "WRITE-AHEAD LOG" above the notebook in the left panel, "RECOVERY" at the top of the right panel.

key: A crab walking down a ladder
name: ch05_crab_latch_ladder
alt: A crab climbs down a ladder gripping the next rung before letting go of the one above.
scene: A clean side view of a tall wooden ladder leaning against a whitewashed wall by the sea, with soft blue sky and a hint of beach behind. A large, friendly orange crab with expressive eyes climbs down the ladder. Its lower claw has just closed firmly on the next rung down, drawn with a small glowing ring of grip, while its upper claw is opening and releasing the rung above, with a small curved release arrow. Above the crab, two rungs it has already let go of are shown faded with tiny dotted circles where it once held. In a small inset bubble on the right, the same crab holds two rungs at once with a slightly worried expression, and a tiny cracked rung icon below shows why: the rung below might split. The evenly spaced rungs give a clear sense of descent. Bright, cheerful daylight. At the foot of the ladder, a small pail and spade sit in the sand, and a second crab waits patiently at the bottom, looking up and ready to climb only after the first crab has safely moved down. Labels: "LATCH" beside the gripping lower claw, "RELEASE" beside the opening upper claw, "CRABBING" at the top of the ladder.

key: Writers draw the new version on
name: ch06_two_whiteboards_flip
alt: Readers look at a whiteboard tagged current while a writer draws the new version on a second board, ready to flip the tag.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a bright meeting room with two whiteboards side by side on the wall. The left whiteboard carries a magnetic tag reading "current" and shows a finished, tidy diagram of boxes and arrows; three readers (a young woman in a yellow kurti with a notebook, an older man in a sweater vest, a college intern with headphones round his neck) sit in chairs facing it, calmly taking notes. At the right whiteboard, tagged "next", a writer (early 30s, rolled sleeves, marker in hand, absorbed) draws an updated diagram. A curved arrow above both boards shows the "current" tag about to jump from left to right in one motion. In a small inset bubble in the corner, a cleaner with a duster waits patiently at the door of the room, glancing at a wall clock, until the last reader of the old board walks out, before wiping it. Soft natural light, calm and orderly mood. On a side table sit a tray of marker pens and a coffee pot, and a wall clock above the door shows that the readers have been quietly working for some time without being disturbed. Labels: "COPY-ON-WRITE" at the top of the scene, "ATOMIC SWAP" along the curved arrow over the tag.

key: A printed price list on the shop wall
name: ch06_price_list_sticky_notes
alt: A shop wall price list with sticky notes beside it, and at closing time a shopkeeper reprints the list with the notes folded in.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle, inside a small Indian sweet shop with glass display cases of laddoos and jalebis. LEFT panel, daytime: a printed price list is pinned on the wall, and several bright yellow sticky notes are stuck beside it with short scribbled changes; a customer (30s, office bag on shoulder) reads the list and the notes together, eyes moving between them along a small dotted line. The shop owner (50s, white kurta, sandalwood tilak) serves a box of sweets. RIGHT panel, at closing time with the shutter half-down and a warm lamp: the owner sits at the counter with a small printer, peeling off the sticky notes and placing them into a pile; out of the printer come two fresh sheets of the price list, because the updated list no longer fits on one sheet, and a small arrow shows one sheet splitting into two. Bright daylight on the left, warm evening glow on the right. In the left panel a steel weighing scale and a stack of sweet boxes sit on the counter, and in the right panel the old printed list lies on the counter with a fresh one being pinned up. Labels: "BUFFER" next to the sticky notes, "MERGE" over the printer in the right panel.

key: Letters land in the national tray
name: ch06_sorting_office_cascade
alt: A postal sorting office where a full national tray is emptied into regional trays, then into street bags delivered one street at a time.
scene: A cutaway, slightly elevated view of a large Indian postal sorting hall arranged top to bottom like a waterfall. At the top, a single wide wooden tray marked with a small map outline overflows with letters; a sorter (40s, khaki postal uniform, cap) tips it forward. A thick arrow pours the letters down into a middle row of four smaller regional trays. Another sorter (late 20s, same uniform, spectacles) tips one full regional tray into a bottom row of canvas street bags with drawstrings. At the bottom right, a postman (30s, khaki uniform, bicycle with a bag on the carrier) rides out the door with one full bag toward a single street of houses, one visit for many letters. Cascading arrows link all three levels, and a small inset shows one house receiving a thick bundle at once. Even warm light through skylights, busy but orderly mood. Large ceiling fans turn above the hall, and wooden pigeonhole racks line the side walls with small region tags, giving a sense of a large but well-run operation working in stages. Labels: "ROOT BUFFER" beside the top tray, "CHILD BUFFERS" beside the middle row, "LEAF" beside the street bag on the bicycle.

key: a single index card saying
name: ch06_correction_slips_bw_tree
alt: Correction slips are clipped to a ledger page, and a clerk swaps a single index card pointing to the newest slip in one motion.
scene: A close, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an accounts office desk. On the left an open ledger page labelled "page 17" has a small stack of paper correction slips clipped to its top edge with a binder clip, each slip showing a short one-line fix, stacked like a little paper chain. On the right, a wooden card box holds index cards; one card is drawn large and reads "17 → slip 942". A clerk (late 20s, light green shirt, focused) lifts that card out and drops a new one in with a single quick motion, motion lines showing the swap is one move. In a small inset bubble in the corner, a second clerk (30s, glasses) looks surprised because his own card swap lost the race; he clips his slip on top of the stack and reaches to try again, with a small circular retry arrow. Neutral office light, brisk mood. On the wall behind the desk hangs a calendar and a small whiteboard of page numbers, and a teacup steams beside the ledger, showing the clerks work in parallel without waiting on a lock. Labels: "DELTA CHAIN" beside the clipped slips, "MAPPING TABLE" above the card box, "COMPARE-AND-SWAP" beside the swapping hand.

key: the order rail in the kitchen (memtable)
name: ch07_waiter_notepad_order_rail
alt: A waiter writes an order on his notepad before clipping it to the kitchen rail; when the rail falls, the notepad still holds every order.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle, set at the pass window between a restaurant dining room and its kitchen. LEFT panel: a waiter (mid 20s, black vest over a white shirt, small notepad and pencil) writes an order on his pad first, the visible line "2 dosa", then clips a torn copy onto a horizontal steel order rail where several slips already hang in a neat row; a cook in a white cap reads them. A small numbered marker 1 points to the pad and 2 points to the rail. RIGHT panel: the steel rail has fallen off its brackets and the slips are scattered on the floor, a cook throwing up his hands in surprise, while the waiter calmly holds up his notepad showing every order still written in it, with a reassuring smile. Warm, busy restaurant lighting with steam from the kitchen. In the dining room behind the waiter, families sit at tables with steel tumblers of water, and in the right panel one fallen slip lies face-up so the reader can see it matches the notepad entry. Labels: "WAL" beside the notepad, "MEMTABLE" above the order rail in the left panel.

key: Receipts in a shoebox. Every evening
name: ch07_shoebox_receipts_compaction
alt: A woman drops sorted bundles of receipts into a shoebox each evening and, at the weekend, merges them into one sorted folder.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, on a dining table at home. LEFT panel, evening: a young woman (late 20s, cotton night suit, hair clipped up) drops a small rubber-banded bundle of sorted receipts into an open shoebox that already holds several similar bundles stacked newest on top, each bundle with a tiny day tag such as "Mon", "Tue", "Wed". She searches for one receipt by flipping through bundles from the top down, a small numbered order 1, 2, 3 above them. RIGHT panel, weekend morning with sunlight: the same woman sits cross-legged on the floor with all the bundles spread out, merging them into one thick, neatly tabbed folder; empty rubber bands lie around, and the old shoebox is nearly empty. A large arrow flows from the bundles into the folder. Soft lamplight on the left, bright morning light on the right, satisfied mood. A small calculator and a pen lie beside the shoebox, and in the right panel a cup of filter coffee sits on the floor next to her, with the finished folder showing neat alphabetical tabs along its edge. Labels: "FLUSH" above the shoebox, "COMPACTION" above the folder on the right.

key: A relay handover. The new runner
name: ch07_relay_memtable_switch
alt: Two relay runners share the track during a baton handover, and only after the baton is safely passed is a notebook page torn out.
scene: A wide side view of a red running track at a school sports day, with a small crowd and bunting in the background. Two relay runners run side by side in the handover zone: the outgoing runner (late teens, blue vest, number on chest, slowing down, focused) still holds a baton, and the incoming runner (late teens, orange vest, already in full stride, looking back) reaches for it. The baton is drawn mid-handover, gripped by both hands for a moment. At the far edge of the zone stands a small official table where a referee (40s, white cap, whistle) stamps a sheet; a dotted arrow leads from the baton to a filing tray marked with a small disk icon. Next to the table, an assistant tears one page out of a notebook and drops it into a bin, but only after the stamp is done, shown by small numbered markers 1 and 2. Bright sunny daylight, energetic mood. Lane lines and white handover-zone markings are painted clearly on the track, and in the stands a few parents cheer with raised arms while a teacher holds a stopwatch near the table. Labels: "OLD MEMTABLE" above the blue runner, "NEW MEMTABLE" above the orange runner, "FLUSHED" next to the stamped sheet.

key: A wall of light switches. Each key
name: ch07_bloom_filter_switches
alt: A wall of light switches where each key flips three switches, and checking a key means seeing whether all its switches are on.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a long wall panel of sixteen old-style white light switches in a row, in a tidy electrical room. Some switches are flipped on and glow with small orange indicator dots. On the left, a young engineer (mid 20s, maroon hoodie, ID card) adds a key: three thin coloured lines from a small card in his hand marked "X" reach to three specific switches, which flip on. On the right, a second engineer (late 30s, grey shirt, spectacles, clipboard) checks a different card marked "Y": two of its three lines land on switches that are on, but one lands on a switch that is clearly off, with a small green tick beside it. A third faint card marked "Z" has all three lines landing on switches that other keys flipped on, with a big question mark floating above it. Clean, cool lighting, curious mood. Along the top of the panel, each switch has a tiny number plate from 1 to 16, and a small fuse box and coiled cable hang on the side wall to set the scene as a plain electrical room. Labels: "BLOOM FILTER" above the wall, "MAYBE" beside the question mark, "NO" beside the off switch.

key: Two clerks update one paper ledger
name: ch08_two_clerks_lost_update
alt: Two clerks each copy the same ledger balance onto notepads and compute separately, so whoever writes last wipes out the other one's work.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of an old cooperative bank office with wooden tables, a ceiling fan and a wall clock. In the centre, on a stand, lies a large open paper ledger with a balance cell showing "₹1". Two clerks sit on either side. Clerk A on the left (late 30s, white half-sleeve shirt, moustache, spectacles) copies the balance onto a small notepad and writes "+2" beside it; clerk B on the right (early 30s, light pink salwar kameez, pen behind ear) copies the same "₹1" onto her own notepad and writes "×2". Two dotted arrows lead from the ledger to both notepads at the same moment, marked with a tiny matching clock icon on each. In the foreground, clerk B is leaning over to write her result into the ledger, while clerk A, in a small inset bubble, watches his own earlier figure being overwritten, with a puff of smoke where his number vanishes. Neither looks careless; both look puzzled. Warm afternoon office light, mildly comic tension. Labels: "READ" on the dotted arrows to the notepads, "LOST UPDATE" beside the vanishing number in the inset.

key: A ticket counter where the clerk serves
name: ch08_ticket_counter_backpressure
alt: A ticket counter with one clerk and a long rope-barrier queue, and a sign at the entrance telling newcomers the line is full.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a railway reservation hall with a single ticket window and a clerk (50s, grey uniform shirt, steady and unhurried) serving one passenger at a time through the grille. In front of the window a long zigzag rope barrier snakes back and forth across the hall, packed with people: students with backpacks, an elderly couple, a man with a suitcase, a mother with a toddler. The person at the very back of the line (late 20s, office shirt, checking a wristwatch) looks exhausted, with a small clock icon above him showing a long wait. The clerk works at the same pace, shown by a small speedometer icon above the window that does not change. At the hall entrance on the right, an attendant (30s, cap) holds up a sign reading "line full, come back later", and a newly arriving man turns around early, looking mildly annoyed but not stuck. Hazy fluorescent light, crowded but orderly mood. Labels: "QUEUE" along the rope barrier, "BACKPRESSURE" above the sign at the entrance.

key: A company splits into two offices
name: ch08_two_offices_split_brain
alt: Two travel offices cut off from each other by a broken phone line each sell the last ten flight seats, selling twenty in total.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a jagged crack, with a telephone line strung across the top between two small travel agency offices and visibly snapped in the middle, its loose ends sparking. LEFT office: a travel agent (early 30s, blue shirt, headset) cheerfully hands printed tickets to a queue of customers, with a small whiteboard behind him reading "seats left: 10" being counted down. RIGHT office: another agent (late 20s, green kurti, headset) does exactly the same with her own queue and her own whiteboard reading "seats left: 10". A small inset bubble at the bottom shows the line repaired later and a single airplane with ten seats while a crowd of twenty passengers with tickets stands confused at the gate. Both agents look confident and busy, unaware of each other. Bright office light in both halves, the inset in a slightly dimmer tone. Each office has a small window showing the same city skyline, and on each counter sits an identical seat chart of the same flight, with ten seats being ticked off independently in each. Labels: "PARTITION" at the break in the phone line, "SPLIT BRAIN" above the confused crowd in the inset.

key: Partially synchronous: Indian Railways
name: ch08_three_timing_models
alt: Three railway platforms side by side: a perfectly on-time train, a usually on-time Indian train, and a platform with no timetable at all.
scene: A wide triptych illustration divided into three vertical panels, each showing a railway platform at the same moment. LEFT panel: a spotless platform with a large clock and a timetable board, a sleek train arriving exactly as the clock hand hits the hour; a station master (50s, crisp white uniform) nods confidently. MIDDLE panel: a busy Indian platform with a tea vendor, porters in red shirts and families on luggage; a departure board flickers, a train is visible far down the line, and a passenger (30s, checked shirt, holding a chai cup) frowns at his watch, a small question bubble above him with a train and a cross that is faded, showing a guess that may be taken back. RIGHT panel: an empty platform with a blank board where the timetable should be, a single passenger (20s, backpack) sitting on a bench with no idea when or whether a train will come, a big question mark in the sky. Morning light in all three panels. Labels: "SYNCHRONOUS" above the left panel, "PARTIALLY SYNCHRONOUS" above the middle panel, "ASYNCHRONOUS" above the right panel.

key: You phone a friend who always picks up
name: ch09_ringing_phone_timeout
alt: A young woman holds a ringing phone, with a clock showing early, middle and late moments for when to hang up.
scene: A wide, eye-level illustration showing the same young woman (mid 20s, yellow t-shirt, hair in a loose bun) three times along a horizontal timeline, standing in her small apartment living room. On the left at "3 rings" she hangs up too early, and a small inset bubble shows her friend (same age, towel on head) stepping out of a shower toward a ringing phone, labelled with a small red mark. In the middle at "10 rings" she holds the phone to her ear with a worried face, a clock icon showing a few minutes. On the right, at the far end of the timeline, she is still waiting with the phone, slumped, a clock showing an hour, while an inset bubble shows an ambulance siren far away, too late. A horizontal arrow runs under all three positions like a dial, with a highlighted sweet spot between the middle and right positions. Soft evening lamplight, gently tense mood. Her living room has a sofa with cushions, a wall clock and a window with evening light, and the phone screen in each pose shows a growing ring counter so time passing is clear. Labels: "FALSE POSITIVE" above the left inset, "FALSE NEGATIVE" above the right inset, "TIMEOUT" along the arrow.

key: Before reporting them missing you ask
name: ch09_indirect_probe
alt: A man whose call fails asks two colleagues in other buildings to call the same person, and one gets through.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a small office campus with three buildings arranged in a triangle. In the left building, seen through a window, a man (early 30s, white shirt, ID lanyard) holds a desk phone with a frustrated face; a dotted line from his phone toward the far building is broken by a red zigzag. From him two solid arrows go to the other two buildings, where two colleagues pick up their phones: one woman (late 20s, blue kurti) in the top building and one man (40s, grey sweater) in the right building. From each of these colleagues, a dotted line goes to a fourth small building in the background, where the person being called (early 30s, green shirt) sits at his desk perfectly fine, waving and picking up. One of these two lines shows a green tick where the call connects. Daylight with soft shadows, calm problem-solving mood. Each building has a small rooftop water tank and a tree in front, and the broken direct line is drawn crossing a busy road, hinting that the fault lies on the route, not the person. Labels: "PING" on the broken direct line, "INDIRECT PROBE" on the arrows to the two colleagues, "ALIVE" above the person who answers.

key: An office noticeboard copied by hand
name: ch09_gossip_noticeboard
alt: Two colleagues swap hand-copied noticeboards and keep the higher tick count for each name, while one name has not moved in a long time.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of an office corridor with a water cooler and a window. In the centre, two colleagues meet and exchange small cork noticeboards like swapping notebooks: a young man (mid 20s, maroon shirt, lanyard) and a woman (early 30s, beige kurti, spectacles). Each board lists five names with a column of tally ticks beside each. A small inset bubble above them zooms into the boards side by side, with arrows showing the larger tally for each name being copied across. In the background, other colleagues at their desks each hold their own copy of the board and tick their own name with a pencil. One name on every board, "Kiran", has a faded tally with a little cobweb and a small clock icon, showing that nobody has seen it rise for a long time, and Kiran's desk in the far corner is empty with the chair pushed in. Soft daylight, friendly office mood. A potted plant and a printer stand along the corridor, and on the boards the tally marks are drawn as simple clear strokes so the bigger count for each name is easy to see. Labels: "HEARTBEAT COUNTER" beside the tally column in the inset, "SUSPECTED" beside the faded name.

key: A rope team of climbers. If one falls
name: ch09_rope_team_climbers
alt: A rope team of four climbers on a snowy ridge; one slips, the rope goes slack, and the others stop one after another.
scene: A wide side view of a snowy Himalayan ridge under a pale sky, with prayer flags fluttering on a rock in the background and wind streaks blowing snow. Four climbers in bright jackets (red, blue, yellow, green), helmets and crampons are tied together on one long rope, spaced evenly along the ridge from left to right. The lead climber on the far left, in red, has slipped and is sitting in the snow, holding on with an ice axe. The rope near him is drawn slack and drooping. The blue climber next to him has stopped and is tugging the rope, with small motion lines; the yellow climber after him has just felt it and is stopping; the green climber at the far right is still mid-stride but turning his head, with a small curved arrow showing the stop rippling along the rope. Nobody is shouting; small crossed-out speech bubbles above them show the wind drowns voices. Cold, bright light, tense but controlled mood. Labels: "FAILED" above the red climber, "STOP SIGNAL" along the rope, "PROPAGATES" near the rippling arrow.

key: A group of 8 friends planning a trip
name: ch10_trip_planner_leader
alt: Eight friends send trip ideas to one planner who posts the plan, while an inset warns about two planners booking two hotels.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a café table on a terrace with fairy lights, eight friends in their mid 20s sitting around it in casual clothes, phones in hand. At the head of the table one friend (woman, mid 20s, denim jacket, a notebook labelled with a small map) is clearly the planner: seven thin arrows run from the other friends' phones to her notebook, each carrying a tiny idea icon (a beach, mountains, a train), and one thick arrow runs back out from her to everyone carrying a single neat plan card. Everyone looks relaxed. In a small inset bubble at the top right, a contrasting scene: the planner's phone shows a dead battery, and two different friends each hold up booking receipts for two different hotels with startled faces, a jagged split line between them. Warm evening light, friendly mood. Glasses of cold coffee and a plate of fries sit on the table, and a big printed map with a pin and a dotted travel route lies open in front of the planner as she writes the final plan. Labels: "LEADER" under the planner, "FOLLOWERS" near the seven friends, "SPLIT BRAIN" inside the inset.

key: A cricket team where only the vice
name: ch10_cricket_stand_in_captain
alt: On a cricket field the injured captain is helped off while players check three eligible senior players to name a stand-in captain.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a local cricket ground with a dusty pitch, white boundary markers and a small pavilion with a tin roof. On the left, the captain (late 20s, white kit, cap) sits on the grass holding his ankle while a physio kneels beside him with an ice pack. In the centre stand three senior players, each with a small star badge on the chest: the vice-captain (early 30s, beard), the senior batsman (mid 30s, pads on, holding a bat) and the wicket-keeper (late 20s, gloves and pads). Two of them look fit and ready; one has a tiny bandage icon. A young fielder (early 20s) walks over toward them with a questioning gesture. Above the three, small numbered clocks show different waiting times, the most senior having the shortest clock, so his speech bubble with a raised hand appears first while the others hold back. Bright midday sun, purposeful mood. Spectators sit under umbrellas near the pavilion, a scoreboard shows the match paused, and the umpire in a white coat and hat waits patiently near the stumps for the new captain to be named. Labels: "CANDIDATES" above the three starred players, "LEADER" above the player whose speech bubble appears first.

key: A class passing a sign-up sheet along
name: ch10_ring_signup_sheet
alt: Students seated in a circle pass a sign-up sheet around, skipping an absent student, until it returns to the starter who announces the winner.
scene: A top-down, slightly tilted view of a classroom with desks arranged in a circle, eight students in school uniforms (white shirts, navy ties) seated around it. A sheet of paper travels clockwise from desk to desk, shown with curved arrows; each student who has held it has just written their name, with tiny pens in hand. One desk is empty with a small "absent" tag and the arrow skips straight over it to the next student. At the starting desk, a girl (about 15, two plaits) receives the sheet back, reading it, and holds up a small second note to send round, on which "Kiran" is written. In a small inset bubble, a sticky note reads "highest so far" with one name crossed out and a new one written beneath, showing the variant. Soft daylight through windows, cheerful classroom mood. A blackboard with chalk sums and a teacher watching from the doorway with folded arms frame the room, and each student holding the sheet looks briefly at it before passing it on with a nod. Labels: "RING" in the centre of the circle, "ELECTED" next to the second note.

key: A society of 5 flats picks a secretary
name: ch10_society_quorum_secretary
alt: A five-flat building with a broken intercom: two flats try to appoint a secretary but cannot gather three signatures, while three flats sign a dated appointment letter.
scene: A front cutaway view of a small Indian housing society building with five flats stacked two and three, balconies with plants and drying clothes. The intercom panel at the entrance has a broken wire with small sparks, and a jagged line splits the building into a group of two flats on the left and three flats on the right. On the left, two residents (an older man in a vest, a young woman in a kurti) hold a paper with only two signatures and look frustrated, with a small "2/5" note beside it in red. On the right, three residents (a retired uncle with a walking stick, a mother with a toddler, a young man in office wear) gather around a table and sign an appointment letter with a big dated stamp showing a term number "4", and a smiling new secretary (40s, cotton sari, file in hand) receives it. An older letter with a faded term number "3" lies crossed out on the floor. Warm morning light, civic and slightly comic mood. Labels: "QUORUM" above the three signers, "TERM" pointing to the dated stamp on the letter.

key: A partitioned node is a shop whose phone
name: ch11_crashed_vs_partitioned_shop
alt: Two shops side by side: one with shutters down, and one open for business whose phone line to the warehouse has been cut.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, showing two neighbouring small general stores on the same street. LEFT panel: the shop has its metal rolling shutter fully down and padlocked, a hand-written note taped on it; a customer (30s, office bag) shrugs and walks away, mildly disappointed but not cheated. RIGHT panel: the shop is fully open with bright shelves; a cheerful shopkeeper (50s, white vest under an open shirt, towel on shoulder) hands a boxed item to a happy customer (late 20s, kurti, cloth bag) and takes cash. Behind the counter a landline phone's wire runs out the back toward a warehouse in the distance, and the wire is visibly cut with snipped ends. A small inset bubble near the warehouse shows its shelf where that same item's slot is already empty. Even daylight across both panels, with a subtle uneasy tint on the right. Labels: "CRASHED" at the top of the left panel, "PARTITIONED" at the top of the right panel, and "STALE" beside the item being sold.

key: A single scoreboard in a stadium
name: ch11_stadium_scoreboard_linearizable
alt: A cricket stadium with one big scoreboard being updated by a worker on a ladder, and the whole crowd seeing the same number flip at one instant.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a packed cricket stadium from behind the boundary rope, the crowd in colourful shirts waving flags. On the far side stands a single tall manual scoreboard with large painted number plates. A scoreboard worker (40s, cap, white shirt with sleeves rolled) climbs a ladder carrying a new number plate; a dotted path up the ladder shows the climb takes a few seconds, but a small bright flash marks the exact instant the plate swaps from "1" to "2". In the stands, many spectators in different sections all look at the same board, with thin sight-lines from several of them converging on it, showing everyone sees the same value. A second worker waits at the bottom of the ladder with another plate, showing more updates queued. A small inset bubble near one spectator shows her thought bubble "2", with an old "1" crossed out and a tiny arrow pointing only forward. Bright afternoon sunshine, lively mood. Labels: "LINEARIZABLE" above the scoreboard, "ONE INSTANT" beside the flash on the plate.

key: RIFL is a coat-check ticket
name: ch11_coat_check_ticket
alt: At a coat-check counter, a guest hands in his coat again after the attendant faints, and the attendant looks up the ticket instead of hanging a second copy.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, at the coat-check counter of a wedding banquet hall with chandeliers and racks of hanging coats. LEFT panel: a guest (early 30s, dark sherwani) hands over his coat; the attendant (late 20s, waistcoat and bow tie) has fainted sideways onto a stool, cartoon stars above his head, before handing over a ticket. RIGHT panel: the attendant, now recovered, is checking a ledger with rows like "client 7, item 12", one row ticked; the same guest hands the coat over a second time, and the attendant smiles and hands back a numbered ticket while the rack shows only one coat on hook 12, no duplicate. A small ghosted inset bubble shows what would have happened without tickets: a second identical coat hung over another guest's coat, crossed out in red. Warm golden banquet light, gently comic mood. A small brass bell sits on the counter and rows of numbered hooks run along the back wall, most of them holding coats and shawls, with hook 12 clearly visible in both panels. Labels: "RETRY" above the left panel, "DEDUP" next to the ledger in the right panel.

key: Three notebooks. A writer must update
name: ch11_quorum_three_notebooks
alt: A writer updates two of three notebooks and a reader checks two of three, and their piles always share at least one notebook with the newest entry.
scene: A wide, top-down view of a long wooden table with three identical notebooks laid in a row, labelled 1, 2 and 3 by small tabs. On the left, a writer (early 30s, blue checked shirt, pen in hand) has just written in notebooks 1 and 2; two orange arrows from his pen land on them, and each now shows a fresh line with a small version tag "v5". Notebook 3 still shows an older line "v4". On the right, a reader (late 20s, green kurti, spectacles) has picked up notebooks 2 and 3; two teal arrows go from her hands to them. Notebook 2 is touched by both orange and teal arrows and glows softly, with a small circle around it. In a small inset bubble above the reader, she compares the two versions side by side and picks "v5" with a tick. Soft, even daylight, calm puzzle-solving mood. A desk lamp and a pen stand sit at the far end of the table, and each notebook is open to the same page so the version tags at the top are easy to compare side by side. Labels: "W=2" above the orange arrows, "R=2" above the teal arrows, "OVERLAP" beside the glowing notebook 2.

key: A school sends news home. Broadcast
name: ch12_school_news_three_ways
alt: Three ways a school spreads news: the principal phoning every parent, parents comparing notes at the gate, and parents each phoning two others.
scene: A wide triptych illustration divided into three vertical panels, each set around the same Indian school with a painted gate and a banyan tree. LEFT panel: the principal (50s, cotton sari, spectacles, phone to her ear) sits at her desk with a long list of numbers, looking tired and feverish with a thermometer in her mouth; half the names on the list are ticked and half are not. MIDDLE panel: at the school gate in the morning, a cluster of parents (a father on a scooter, a mother with a lunch box, a grandfather holding a child's hand) chat and compare small notes, with tiny arrows passing information between them. RIGHT panel: a branching tree of small phone icons spreading from one parent to two, then to four, then to eight, each parent drawn as a small figure on a phone, spreading quickly across the panel even though the principal's figure at the root is faded out. Bright morning light, everyday community mood. Labels: "BROADCAST" above the left panel, "ANTI-ENTROPY" above the middle panel, "GOSSIP" above the right panel.

key: your neighbour signs for it
name: ch12_hinted_handoff_neighbour
alt: A courier leaves a parcel with a neighbour who adds a sticky note for flat B, and later hands it over when the owner returns home.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle, set in the corridor of an Indian apartment building with two facing doors marked "A" and "B", shoe racks and a potted tulsi plant. LEFT panel, afternoon: door B is locked with a small padlock; a courier (late 20s, red cap, uniform t-shirt, handheld scanner) hands a parcel to the neighbour from flat A (60s, retired uncle in a vest and lungi, spectacles), who sticks a yellow note reading "for flat B" on it. A small inset bubble shows the owner of flat B at an office desk, being asked about the parcel and shrugging, unaware. RIGHT panel, evening: the owner of flat B (early 30s, office clothes, laptop bag) has just come home; the neighbour hands the parcel across the corridor with a smile, and peels off the sticky note, dropping it into a small dustbin. Warm afternoon light on the left, soft evening tube light on the right, friendly mood. A doormat sits outside each door and a delivery bike is visible through a window at the end of the corridor, while in the right panel a wall clock shows the late evening hour. Labels: "HINT" beside the sticky note, "HANDOFF" above the right panel.

key: Two libraries want to know if their
name: ch12_merkle_libraries
alt: Two library buildings compare fingerprints for the building, then aisles, then shelves, narrowing down to one mismatching shelf.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of two identical library buildings side by side, each with a cutaway front showing two aisles inside, and each aisle with two shelves of books. Above each building floats a fingerprint card connected by thin lines to two aisle fingerprint cards, each connected to two shelf fingerprint cards, forming a small upside-down tree of cards over each building. Two librarians (left: 40s, woman in a blue sari with a clipboard; right: 50s, man in a brown jacket with spectacles) stand between the buildings comparing cards. The top building cards differ, marked with a small red cross; they then compare the aisle cards, where one pair matches with a green tick and the other differs; then only that aisle's shelf cards, finding one mismatching shelf highlighted with a glowing outline and a few books pulled out on a trolley. A dotted path shows the comparison going down only the mismatching branch. Calm daylight, methodical mood. Labels: "MERKLE TREE" above the card trees, "MISMATCH" beside the highlighted shelf.

key: A phone tree for a sports club
name: ch12_phone_tree_broken_branch
alt: A sports club phone tree where the captain calls two people who each call two more, and one dead phone cuts off a whole branch.
scene: A wide illustration laid out as a tree from top to bottom on a pale green background suggesting a sports field. At the top, the club captain (late 20s, football jersey with an armband, phone to ear) calls two players below him, drawn with solid arrows. Each of those calls two more players, and so on, making three neat levels of small figures in matching club jerseys, each holding a phone, with green ticks beside those who received the call. On the right side, one player in the middle level holds a phone with a dead battery icon and a sad face; the arrows below him are grey and dashed, and the three players beneath him stand puzzled with question marks, cut off. In a small inset bubble at the bottom right, one of those cut-off players on a Friday checks with a teammate from another branch at the practice nets, catching the news. Bright, sporty daylight. Goalposts and a few footballs appear faintly along the bottom edge, and each level of the tree is spaced evenly so the doubling of callers at each step is easy to read. Labels: "BROADCAST TREE" at the top, "DEAD BRANCH" beside the grey dashed arrows, "GOSSIP REPAIR" inside the inset.

key: A wedding officiant (coordinator)
name: ch13_wedding_two_phase_commit
alt: A wedding officiant asks bride and groom in turn, and only after two firm yeses pronounces them married.
scene: A wide, eye-level view of a decorated Indian wedding mandap with marigold garlands, a small sacred fire and guests seated on chairs in the background. In the centre stands the officiant (60s, white dhoti and kurta, shawl, spectacles, kindly face) holding a small book. To his left stands the groom (late 20s, cream sherwani, turban) and to his right the bride (late 20s, red lehenga, jewellery). Speech bubbles show the sequence: above the officiant a question mark bubble directed to each, then two bubbles from the groom and bride each with a firm tick, each tick drawn with a small padlock to show the promise cannot be taken back. Above the officiant a final big bubble with two joined rings shows the pronouncement, appearing only after both ticks. In a small inset bubble in the corner, a contrasting scene shows one partner shaking their head and the officiant closing his book, with everyone free to leave. Warm festive golden light, joyful mood. Labels: "PREPARE" above the two tick bubbles, "COMMIT" above the rings bubble, "ABORT" inside the inset.

key: If mission control goes silent during
name: ch13_rocket_three_phase_commit
alt: A mission control room polls launch stations, arms them, then launches, with stations finishing the countdown on their own once all are armed.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of a rocket launch site at dawn: on the left, a mission control room with rows of consoles and a large window; on the right, a tall rocket on a launch pad flanked by four small ground stations, each with one engineer in an orange jumpsuit and headset. Inside mission control, a flight director (40s, white shirt, headset, clipboard) speaks into a microphone. Three stacked speech bubbles drift from him toward the stations in sequence: the first with a question mark, the second with a lightning bolt showing arming, the third with a flame showing launch. Each station shows a small panel with a green light; all four are lit. A small inset bubble shows the flight director's microphone with a static crackle and silence, while all four station engineers, each knowing the others are armed, calmly watch a shared countdown clock reaching zero. Cool dawn light with orange glow on the horizon, focused mood. Labels: "PROPOSE" beside the first bubble, "PREPARE" beside the second, "COMMIT" beside the third.

key: An orchestra spread over three cities
name: ch13_orchestra_shared_score
alt: Musicians in three cities play the same agreed score at the same moment over video, without phoning each other between bars.
scene: A wide triptych illustration divided into three vertical panels, each a small rehearsal room in a different Indian city, suggested through the window: sea and a skyline in the left room, old domes in the middle, and green hills on the right. In each room one musician plays: a violinist (woman, late 20s, green kurta), a tabla player (man, 40s, white kurta), a flautist (young man, early 20s, black t-shirt). Each has an identical printed score on a stand, opened to the same page, with a bright bar highlighted at the same place. Above all three panels, a thin horizontal timeline runs across with a single "play" marker, and dotted lines drop down from it into each room at the same instant. In the middle panel, a small crossed-out phone icon floats to show they do not call each other. In a small inset bubble in the right panel, the flautist has fainted onto a chair and, recovered, reads the score to catch up while the other rooms play on. Warm indoor light, harmonious mood. Labels: "SHARED LOG" above the score stands, "DETERMINISTIC" along the top timeline.

key: A round table with name cards
name: ch13_round_table_consistent_hashing
alt: Guests around a round table sit at the first name card clockwise from where they stand, and adding a new card moves only a few guests.
scene: A top-down view of a large round banquet table with a white cloth, ringed by evenly spaced chairs, in a hall with a tiled floor. Four name cards in folded stand-up style are placed at a few seats around the table, each a different colour (red, blue, green, yellow). Small guest figures in festive clothes stand at various points around the table edge, each with a short curved arrow showing them walking clockwise to the nearest name card, so the guests form coloured groups. A waiter (30s, black waistcoat) is placing a brand new purple name card between the red and blue cards. Only the two guests standing just before it, between the red card and the new purple card, are drawn with brighter outlines and small curved arrows switching to the purple card; all other guests stay calmly in place with tiny ticks. Warm overhead chandelier light, orderly mood. The tablecloth edge is marked with faint tick marks around the circle like a clock dial, and plates and glasses are set at every chair to emphasise that seats are fixed positions. Labels: "HASH RING" in the centre of the table, "NEW NODE" beside the purple card, "MOVED KEYS" beside the two switching guests.

key: A ship changing captains. First the new
name: ch14_ship_captain_zab
alt: A new ship captain gathers officers' logbooks, copies the most complete one into all of them, then gives new orders that most officers acknowledge.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of the deck and open bridge of a cargo ship on a calm sea, gulls overhead. Read left to right as three moments. LEFT: the new captain (late 40s, woman, navy uniform with four gold stripes, cap under arm) stands with four officers in white uniforms, each holding up a logbook toward her, small bubbles above them showing different last entry numbers. CENTRE: at a chart table, she copies pages from the thickest logbook into the others, arrows showing the copying, until all four logbooks are the same height. RIGHT: on the bridge she speaks an order through a brass voice pipe, and three of the four officers nod with green ticks, while one is still turning toward her. On the deck floor, a small torn sheet stamped with an older voyage number "1" is being swept overboard by the wind. Bright sea daylight, disciplined mood. A ship bell, coiled ropes and a life ring hang along the railing, and the logbooks are drawn with clear spines so the difference in thickness before and after copying is obvious. Labels: "DISCOVERY" above the left moment, "SYNCHRONIZATION" above the centre, "BROADCAST" above the right moment.

key: Booking a meeting room through three
name: ch14_paxos_receptionists
alt: A man phones three receptionists to hold a meeting room with request number seven, and must book an earlier meeting someone already pencilled in.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated view of three reception desks in a row in a shared office building lobby, each with a receptionist wearing a headset: a young woman in a blue blazer, an older man with a grey moustache, and a woman in a printed kurti. In the foreground a young professional (late 20s, light shirt, lanyard, laptop under arm) holds his phone and a small card reading "#7". Two thin arrows go from him to the first two desks, a majority, each receptionist writing on a booking pad. The second receptionist holds up her pad showing a pencilled entry "Priya", and a small curved arrow shows the man crossing out his own meeting topic on his card and writing in Priya's meeting instead. In a small inset bubble on the right, the third receptionist holds up a card reading "#8" promised to someone else and shakes her head at a later "#7" request. Bright, clean office light, careful mood. Labels: "PREPARE" along the first arrows, "PROMISE" beside the receptionists' pads, "ACCEPT" beside the man's corrected card.

key: Multi-Paxos elects a secretary once
name: ch14_multi_paxos_secretary_lease
alt: A meeting room where one elected secretary writes minutes line after line, each confirmed by nods, with a wall clock showing her ten-minute lease.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided down the middle by a thin vertical line, inside a cooperative society meeting room with a long table. LEFT panel: chaos of repeated elections, with members raising hands and passing ballot slips for every single sentence of the minutes, a tired chairman (60s, white kurta) tallying votes, a ballot box overflowing. RIGHT panel: calm. One secretary (late 30s, lavender sari, spectacles, pen) sits at the head of the table writing line after line in a minutes book; around the table, most members nod gently, each nod drawn with a small green tick beside the line being written. On the wall above her hangs a clock with a highlighted ten-minute wedge, and a small badge on her desk shows a padlock with a clock, showing she alone may take minutes for now. In a small inset, two members compare their wristwatches which disagree slightly, with a question mark. Soft daylight, orderly mood. Labels: "CLASSIC PAXOS" at the top of the left panel, "MULTI-PAXOS" at the top of the right panel, "LEASE" beside the wall clock.

key: A shared kitchen without a head chef
name: ch14_shared_kitchen_epaxos
alt: In a shared kitchen with no head chef, one person makes toast and another tea freely, while two cooks reaching for the only frying pan must agree who goes first.
scene: A wide, slightly elevated three-quarter view of a shared hostel kitchen with tiled walls, steel shelves and a window. There is no head chef. On the left, a young woman (early 20s, hoodie, hair tied up) makes toast at a toaster, and a young man (early 20s, glasses, t-shirt) brews tea in a steel pan on a separate burner; both work happily without talking, each with a small green tick above them. On the right, two more cooks, a young man (mid 20s, apron) and a young woman (mid 20s, apron, holding a bowl of pancake batter), both reach for the only frying pan hanging on the wall at the same time, hands nearly touching, with a small spark between them. A small note on the wall between them reads "omelette after pancakes", with an arrow showing the agreed order. Warm morning light through the window, friendly and lively mood. A whiteboard on the fridge shows a simple chore rota, and a kettle and a jar of tea leaves sit on the counter, emphasising that this is a shared space where people organise their own dishes. Labels: "NO LEADER" above the scene, "INDEPENDENT" above the toast and tea cooks, "CONFLICT" above the frying pan.
